body:
Step B2 of the multi-account design (, sections 4 and 5, without the local area).
First user-visible step: several servers in one app.

* **Start screen** (no account yet): Sign in · Register, both today's login form. The third
  option arrives in B3. Login/registration create an account through B1's `AuthRepository`.
* **Accounts screen** under Settings: rows with label, email, state (signed in · signed out, tap
  to sign in again · app too old for this server); add account (login form; refusing a duplicate
  (server, account) pair with a message); rename label; reorder; remove. Removal reuses the
  existing warning dialog and adds the sentence about copying lists to the local area first
  (the local area itself comes in B3; until then the sentence reads "copy them to another
  account"). Nothing automatic. Unpushed-changes warning as today.
* **Overview**: single account → unchanged. Several → sections headed by account label in
  `sortOrder`, per-card indicator, pending invites under their account, account picker in the
  New-list dialog (default: account of the last opened list). Sync status chip shows the
  worst-of aggregate; tapping it opens Accounts, where each account shows its own.
* **List screen**: unchanged except the app-bar subtitle with several accounts.
* **Update required** (T-244) becomes per account: an outdated account is disabled with an
  explanation on the Accounts screen and its section on the overview shows a one-line notice;
  the full-screen block appears only when every server account is outdated.
* **Invite links**: match by host as in section 5; no match → add-account form pre-filled with
  the server URL, then redeem. Redeem screen names the account it will redeem into when there
  are several.
* **Per-account settings**: default currency and notification preference move under the
  account row; the old top-level entries go.
* Remove B1's `CurrentAccount` shim: every view model receives the account explicitly.
* Strings in all nine locales; `crossClient.test.ts` needs no change (Android-only strings do
  not pair). **AGENTS.md** gets the parity exception recorded: account management is Android-only
  because the web client is always one account on one server.
* Screen tests: Accounts screen (states, remove dialog text), overview with one vs. two
  accounts (headers only with two), new-list picker, invite-link routing with zero/one/two
  matching accounts, update-required per account vs. all.
title: Android: several accounts in the UI: start screen, Accounts screen, grouped overview, invite routing (B2)
